# Programa — Style Reference

> Felt-pen sticky notes on a linen studio desk, one mint key. A weight-300 serif headlines a warm-gray Inter interface on white and linen, 1px rings at 8% black draw every edge, and a single mint tab marks the way in.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Programa speaks a warm-paper studio language. The canvas is Paper Canvas #ffffff, cards sit on Linen Surface #fcfbf9, broad bands drop to Parchment Wash #f8f6f3, and one testimonial slab inverts to Jet Panel #000000. The chromatic budget is exactly two hues: Mint Signal #a7f3d0 on the single nav key and the "New" badge, and Sunbeam Highlight #fdffa2 used once. The hero photograph and product mockups carry every other color. Typography is the thesis. Rhymes Display at weight 300 sets the display line at 80px on 64px leading with -1.5px tracking, a light serif that speaks quietly at a size where convention shouts in a bold sans. Inter at 400 and 500 runs the interface on a 12–24px ladder close to a Minor Third, and uppercase Roboto Mono labels add a third, technical voice. Shapes stay soft at 6–8px. Elevation is a 1px ring at 8% black plus a 1–2px contact shadow. The whole reads as an interiors magazine wrapped around a spreadsheet rather than a SaaS dashboard dressed up for marketing.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |

| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page body, secondary button fill, award-badge strip and inverted text on dark fills (33 fills, 41 text uses). It is the neutral stage that lets the photographic hero hold all the warmth. |
| Linen Surface | `#fcfbf9` | `--color-linen-surface` | Fill for all six feature cards and their mockup trays (24 uses). It sits one barely-visible step off white, so cards are defined by their ring rather than their fill. |
| Parchment Wash | `#f8f6f3` | `--color-parchment-wash` | Full-width bands below the hero and quieter section backgrounds (5 uses). The warm undertone ties the software to fabric and paper samples. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffffb3` | `--color-frosted-glass` | The feature dropdown panel over the hero, paired with a 20px backdrop blur. It lets the collage show through the menu. Do not use it on flat white sections, where it is invisible. |
| Jet Panel | `#000000` | `--color-jet-panel` | The single testimonial slab carrying a white serif quote. It is the only true black on the page, so a customer's voice gets one deliberate full inversion. |
| Carbon Fill | `#2b2926` | `--color-carbon-fill` | Compact "Get started" buttons inside section blocks, with a matching 1px border (5 uses). It is a warm near-black that is softer than Ink at small sizes. |
| Ink | `#1a1916` | `--color-ink` | All headlines, nav links, card titles and the hero primary button fill (60 text uses). Its brown-black cast keeps type warm instead of the blue-black that is standard in SaaS. |
| Pebble Caption | `#7b736c` | `--color-pebble-caption` | Card subtitles, hero subcopy, mono eyebrows and footer links. It is the most-used text color at 85 uses, so secondary voice outnumbers primary voice. |
| Stone Hairline | `#eeece6` | `--color-stone-hairline` | 1px dividers, card internals and footer rules (24 border uses). It is a warm hairline that separates without the cold gray of a default border. |
| Mint Signal | `#a7f3d0` | `--color-mint-signal` | The nav "Start free" fill and its own 1px ring (2 uses). It is the one saturated action color, kept for the persistent entry point. Do not promote it to section CTAs or headline color. |
| Mint Wash | `#d1fae5` | `--color-mint-wash` | Background of the "New" badge inside the feature menu (2 uses). It is a paler echo of Mint Signal that marks novelty without competing with the CTA. |
| Forest Ink | `#064e3b` | `--color-forest-ink` | Text on Mint Wash badges (2 uses). It is the only colored text on the page and stays legible on mint without falling back to Ink. |
| Sunbeam Highlight | `#fdffa2` | `--color-sunbeam-highlight` | A single highlight fill with a matching 1px border, which echoes the yellow sticky note in the hero. It is rationed to one use. Do not use it for links in running text. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Rhymes Display — the light editorial serif that carries every section headline · `--font-rhymes-display`

- **Substitute:** Newsreader Display at 400, Instrument Serif at 400, Libre Caslon Display at 400. Rhymes Display Light draws heavier than its nominal 300 at display sizes and renders closer to a regular, so match it with 400 cuts rather than true lights.
- **Weights:** 300
- **Sizes:** 36px, 44px, 60px, 80px
- **Line height:** 0.8 (80px), 1.07 (60px), 1.14 (44px), 0.94 (36px)
- **Letter spacing:** -1.5px at 80px and 60px; -0.2px at 44px and 36px
- **Role:** A single weight across 16 uses is the signature. The serif never bolds, so headlines gain authority through size and the fashion-editorial cut rather than stroke mass. This inverts the SaaS convention of 600–700 sans headlines. Leading set below the font size (80/64) stacks lines like a magazine masthead. The jump from 44px to 80px is a 1.82 ratio, far wider than a Perfect Fourth, which keeps the H1 a one-off event.

### Inter — the interface workhorse for body, card titles and controls · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400/500 (open source, use the original), Geist at 400/500, Manrope at 400/500 set 1% tighter. Inter renders true to its nominal weight.
- **Weights:** 400, 500
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 16px, 20px, 24px
- **Line height:** 1.33, 1.4, 1.43, 1.5, 1.25
- **Letter spacing:** 0px (normal) at every size
- **Role:** Inter appears 152 times and never goes above 500, so the product voice stays procedural while the serif does the persuading. The 12→14→16→20→24 ladder steps between 1.14 and 1.25, close to a Minor Third and denser than a Major Third. That density suits a tool that shows schedules and SKUs. Tracking stays at normal, which keeps it neutral beside the tightly tracked serif.

### Roboto Mono — uppercase micro-labels and footer column heads · `--font-roboto-mono`

- **Substitute:** Roboto Mono at 400/500 (open source), JetBrains Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400. Roboto Mono renders true to weight.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600
- **Sizes:** 12px
- **Line height:** 1, 1.33, 1.67
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 12px
- **Role:** A single 12px size in uppercase across 29 uses works as a specification-sheet stamp. It names columns like "PRODUCT" and testimonial attributions the way a drawing title block would. Weights 500 and 600 provide emphasis inside the label tier without enlarging it. The pairing reads as studio drawings annotated by an architect, not as developer tooling.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Roboto Mono | 400 | 12px | 1.67 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 400 | 12px | 1.33 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| subheading | Inter | 500 | 20px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Inter | 500 | 24px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Rhymes Display | 300 | 36px | 0.94 | -0.2px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Rhymes Display | 300 | 44px | 1.14 | -0.2px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Rhymes Display | 300 | 80px | 0.8 | -1.5px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every section headline in Rhymes Display weight 300 at 44px with -0.2px tracking — the light serif is the brand's voice, and size alone carries the rank.
- Tighten display leading below the font size: 80px type on 64px leading at -1.5px tracking — stacked lines read as a magazine masthead, not a web H1.
- Keep the interface in Inter 400 and 500 only, from 12px to 24px — the product voice stays procedural so the serif does the persuading.
- Draw edges with the subtle ring, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0 0 0 1px plus a 1px 2px drop at 12% — cards and white buttons are defined by a hairline of shadow, not a border.
- Make Mint Signal #a7f3d0 on the "Start free" nav key the single saturated action — the chromatic budget of two hues is non-negotiable.
- Put secondary copy in Pebble Caption #7b736c at 14px — warm gray at 85 uses is the page's dominant text tone and keeps density calm.
- Pair Ink #1a1916 and Paper Canvas #ffffff buttons at matching 36px height and 6px radius — the two actions read as one control.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis — a heavy Rhymes headline turns the quiet editorial authority into ordinary marketing shouting, and it breaks the 300-only thesis.
- Don't spread mint #a7f3d0 to section CTAs or links — the color identifies the one persistent entry point, and repeating it removes the signal.
- Don't swap Ink #1a1916 for pure #000000 in text — the brown-black cast warms the page, and true black is reserved for the single Jet Panel slab.
- Don't add a 1px #e5e7eb gray border to cards — a cool CSS border fights the warm 8% ring and makes Linen tiles look like default components.
- Don't raise card radii to 16px or 24px — the system tops out at 12px for sections, and soft blobs would read as consumer app rather than studio tool.
- Don't add letter-spacing to Roboto Mono labels beyond 0px — wide-tracked caps at 12px drift into fashion-label territory and lose the drawing-sheet tone.
- Don't fill the nav bar with #ffffff over the hero — the 72px rail is meant to float on the photograph, and a solid band cuts the collage in half. Never let the bar compete with the image.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #fcfbf9 (Linen Surface)
- section band: #f8f6f3 (Parchment Wash)
- primary text: #1a1916 (Ink)
- secondary text: #7b736c (Pebble Caption)
- hairline: #eeece6 (Stone Hairline)
- accent: #a7f3d0 (Mint Signal)
- primary action: #1a1916 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and progress bars stay neutral, with fills in #1a1916 and #7b736c on #eeece6 tracks. Mint #a7f3d0 may mark a single highlighted series only as a solid fill at 100% on at most one bar or line, so the accent never becomes the loudest thing on a page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button pair. The first button: background #1a1916, text #ffffff, no CSS border, border-radius 6px, padding 0 12px, height 36px, Inter 16px weight 400 with line-height 1.5, box-shadow `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) 0px 0.75px 0px 0px inset, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) 0px 1px 2px 0px, rgb(24, 24, 27) 0px 0px 0px 1px`, label "Get started". Place it 6px to the left of a second button: background #ffffff, text #1a1916, radius 6px, padding 0 12px, height 36px, Inter 16px weight 400, box-shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 2px 0px`, label "Watch a demo". No hover color shifts beyond darkening the dark button to #2b2926.

2. Build a Feature Card. It is a 368×368px article with background #fcfbf9, border-radius 8px, overflow hidden, no border, and box-shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 2px 0px`. Inset 20px from top and left, place the title "Specifications" in Inter 20px weight 500 line-height 1.4 color #1a1916, then 2px below it the subtitle "Goodbye spreadsheets, hello Schedules." in Inter 14px weight 400 line-height 1.43 color #7b736c. Fill the lower 60% with a stack of two slightly rotated #ffffff product cards (radius 6px, same subtle shadow) that bleed off the right and bottom edges. Lay six cards in a 3-column grid with 24px gaps inside a 1200px container.

3. Build a Navigation Bar. It is sticky, 72px tall, transparent background, content max-width 1200px with space-between alignment. On the left, a 139×34px wordmark. In the center, links "Features", "Solutions", "Pricing", "Learn" in Inter 14px weight 400 color #1a1916, padding 0 8px, height 28px, border-radius 6px, hover background #ffffffb3. On the right, "Log in" with the same link spec, then a "Start free" key: background #a7f3d0, text #1a1916, Inter 14px weight 500, padding 4px 8px, radius 6px, box-shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) 0px 1px 2px 0px, rgb(167, 243, 208) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) 0px 0.75px 0px 0px inset`.

4. Build a Hero Section. Use a full-bleed, full-viewport photograph of a styled interior desk as the background. Centered at the top, an H1 "Freedom, by design" in Rhymes Display (fallback Newsreader 400) at 80px weight 300, line-height 0.8, letter-spacing -1.5px, color #1a1916. 24px below it, a two-line subline in Inter 16px weight 400 line-height 1.5 color #7b736c, max-width 400px, centered. 20px below that, the Primary Action Button pair from prompt 1. Embed a product screenshot inside the pictured monitor, and do not add overlays, gradients or glows.

5. Build a Testimonial Panel. It is a centered block max-width 1000px with background #000000, border-radius 12px and padding 80px 60px. The quote is in Rhymes Display 44px weight 300 line-height 1.14 letter-spacing -0.2px color #ffffff, centered, max-width 720px. 32px below it, the attribution "SMAC STUDIO · PRINCIPAL DESIGNER · SYDNEY" in Roboto Mono 12px weight 400 uppercase line-height 1.67 color #ffffff. 12px below that, a 40px circular avatar with radius 999px. Place 80px of Paper Canvas #ffffff above and below.

The subtle shadow (a 1px ring at 8% black plus a 1px drop at 12%) replaces a border entirely. It always sits immediately right of the Ink button with a 6px gap. Matching dimensions and type make the pair read as one control with two outcomes rather than a hierarchy of loud and quiet.

### Compact Section CTA Pair — Carbon and Paper

**Role:** In-section actions under feature headlines.

A scaled-down pair. The dark key is #2b2926 fill with a 1px #2b2926 border, #ffffff text and the sm shadow. The light key is #ffffff fill with a 1px #ffffff border, #1a1916 text and the subtle shadow. Both use 6px radius, 6px 8px padding and 31px height in Inter 12px weight 400 on 1.4 leading. Carbon replaces Ink at this size because the warmer #2b2926 keeps a 12px label from looking like a black hole on white.

### Mint Nav Key — Start Free (System Outlier)

**Role:** Persistent sign-up entry in nav.

The only colored action. It is #a7f3d0 fill with #1a1916 text, 6px radius, 4px 8px padding and 28px height in Inter 14px weight 500, with the sm-2 shadow: a mint 1px ring, a 1px drop at 20% black and a 20% white inset. It breaks the neutral-action rule on purpose. The nav key must stay findable over a busy photographic hero, so it gets the whole chromatic budget, and the same mint is not used on any section button.

### Navigation Bar — Sticky Transparent

**Role:** Global wayfinding over the collage.

A thin, floating rail. It is 72px tall, sticky, and has no fill over the hero. The wordmark sits left at 139×34px. Links (Features, Solutions, Pricing, Learn) are Inter 14px weight 400 #1a1916 with 0 8px padding, a 6px hover radius and 28px height. "Log in" and the Mint Nav Key sit right. Leaving out a bar background, which is the common convention, lets the photograph bleed to the top edge, so the menu reads as type laid on the image.

### Glass Feature Menu

**Role:** Dropdown feature index from nav.

A frosted tray. It is #ffffffb3 fill with a 20px backdrop blur, 10px radius, 8px padding and the md-2 shadow (a warm 1px ring at rgba(43, 41, 38, 0.08), a -1px contact drop and a 2px 8px ambient at 10%). Rows pair an Inter 14px weight 500 #1a1916 title with an Inter 14px weight 400 #7b736c descriptor. It is the most elevated surface on the page. The 10px radius, one step above the 8px card radius, signals that it floats above everything else.

### "New" Badge — Mint Wash

**Role:** Novelty flag inside menu rows.

A whispered tag. It is #d1fae5 fill with #064e3b text, 10px radius and 2px 6px padding, in Inter 12px weight 500 on 1.33 leading, with no shadow. It is the only place colored text is allowed. Pairing the pale wash with the deep green keeps it inside the mint family, so it reads as a sibling of the nav key rather than a new hue.

### Feature Card — Linen Tile

**Role:** Primary product-capability card, 3-up grid.

A square specimen tile. It is #fcfbf9 fill, 8px radius and 368×368px, with the subtle shadow (1px ring at 8% black plus 1px drop at 12%) and no CSS border. The title is Inter 20px weight 500 #1a1916 on 1.4 leading, followed by an Inter 14px weight 400 #7b736c subtitle, both inset 20px. Below them a product mockup is cropped against the right and bottom edges. The deliberate bleed tells the visitor the tool extends past the frame, which is conventional for screenshots and unusual for feature cards.

### Testimonial Panel — Jet Slab

**Role:** Single inverted customer-voice moment.

The page's one inversion. It is #000000 fill, 12px radius and roughly 1000px wide, centered, with 80px vertical padding. The quote is Rhymes Display 44px weight 300 #ffffff on 1.14 leading with -0.2px tracking. The attribution is Roboto Mono 12px uppercase #ffffff. The 12px radius, a step above cards, marks it as a section rather than a tile. Use it once per page: two jet slabs would turn punctuation into pattern.

### Award Badge Strip

**Role:** Third-party proof row.

A quiet trust ledger. It is a full-width #ffffff band about 80px tall holding twelve grayscale Capterra, GetApp and Software Advice badges at equal spacing, roughly 40px tall each. The badges' own colors are desaturated to warm grays and treated as decorative, not system tokens. Removing the badges' native reds and blues is intentional: the proof row must not outshout the single mint key.

### Mono Eyebrow Label

**Role:** Section and column micro-headings.

A drafting stamp. It is Roboto Mono 12px weight 400 uppercase in #7b736c on 1.67 leading with 0px tracking, and it steps to weight 500 or 600 for emphasis. It has no background, border or radius and sits 12px above the element it labels. Uppercase mono with no added tracking is anti-convention, since most systems add 0.05em, and it keeps the labels compact like a title block on a drawing set.

### Footer — Ruled Columns

**Role:** Sitemap and legal close.

A lifted sheet. It is full-width, 373px tall, on #ffffff, with the md shadow (2px 8px ambient at 10%, -1px contact drop, 1px ring at 8%) so it rises over the page end. Column heads are Roboto Mono 12px uppercase #7b736c, links are Inter 14px weight 400 #1a1916 with 6px row gaps, and rules are 1px #eeece6. Raising the footer with a shadow instead of darkening it, the usual convention, keeps the last screen in the paper register.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every section headline in Rhymes Display weight 300 at 44px with -0.2px tracking — the light serif is the brand's voice, and size alone carries the rank.
- Tighten display leading below the font size: 80px type on 64px leading at -1.5px tracking — stacked lines read as a magazine masthead, not a web H1.
- Keep the interface in Inter 400 and 500 only, from 12px to 24px — the product voice stays procedural so the serif does the persuading.
- Draw edges with the subtle ring, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0 0 0 1px plus a 1px 2px drop at 12% — cards and white buttons are defined by a hairline of shadow, not a border.
- Make Mint Signal #a7f3d0 on the "Start free" nav key the single saturated action — the chromatic budget of two hues is non-negotiable.
- Put secondary copy in Pebble Caption #7b736c at 14px — warm gray at 85 uses is the page's dominant text tone and keeps density calm.
- Pair Ink #1a1916 and Paper Canvas #ffffff buttons at matching 36px height and 6px radius — the two actions read as one control.

### Don't

- Don't bold the serif to 600 or 700 for emphasis — a heavy Rhymes headline turns the quiet editorial authority into ordinary marketing shouting, and it breaks the 300-only thesis.
- Don't spread mint #a7f3d0 to section CTAs or links — the color identifies the one persistent entry point, and repeating it removes the signal.
- Don't swap Ink #1a1916 for pure #000000 in text — the brown-black cast warms the page, and true black is reserved for the single Jet Panel slab.
- Don't add a 1px #e5e7eb gray border to cards — a cool CSS border fights the warm 8% ring and makes Linen tiles look like default components.
- Don't raise card radii to 16px or 24px — the system tops out at 12px for sections, and soft blobs would read as consumer app rather than studio tool.
- Don't add letter-spacing to Roboto Mono labels beyond 0px — wide-tracked caps at 12px drift into fashion-label territory and lose the drawing-sheet tone.
- Don't fill the nav bar with #ffffff over the hero — the 72px rail is meant to float on the photograph, and a solid band cuts the collage in half. Never let the bar compete with the image.

## Elevation

- **Cards, secondary buttons and icon buttons (53 uses):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12) 0px 1px 2px 0px`
- **Dark buttons, Ink and Carbon:** `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) 0px 0.75px 0px 0px inset, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4) 0px 1px 2px 0px, rgb(24, 24, 27) 0px 0px 0px 1px`
- **Mint nav key:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2) 0px 1px 2px 0px, rgb(167, 243, 208) 0px 0px 0px 1px, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) 0px 0.75px 0px 0px inset`
- **Footer and floating trays (20 uses):** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 2px 8px 0px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 1px 2px -1px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08) 0px 0px 0px 1px`

The rule: every elevated element gets a 1px spread-zero ring first and a contact shadow of 2px blur or less. Only floating layers add the 8px ambient.

## Imagery

The hero is a staged, photographic interior collage. A desk is lit in soft daylight, holding a ceramic vase, a mint lamp, fabric swatches and a monitor. Real sticky notes in yellow and pink carry handwritten lines such as "All new Schedules", which treats marketing copy as studio ephemera. The collage's blues, greens and pinks are decorative and not system tokens. Product imagery is live UI: approval threads and schedule rows inside the monitor, plus cropped mockups bleeding out of 8px Linen cards. These are layered as tilted index cards with 6px image radii and the subtle ring. Avatars are 999px circles. Icons are thin monochrome line glyphs at 16px in #1a1916, with no glow, orb or gradient anywhere. The narrative is that the software lives on a designer's real desk among real materials.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1200px container, and the hero and bands run full-bleed to 1905px. Sections are spaced by 80px by default, with 140–160px around the hero transition. The hero centers an 80px Rhymes headline at the top of a full-viewport photograph, with a 16px #7b736c subline, the Ink and Paper button pair, and the product UI embedded in the pictured monitor. Below it, a Parchment Wash band leads into a 12-up award badge row on white. Feature content follows as a 3-column grid of 368px square Linen cards in two rows with 24px gaps, then a single centered Jet testimonial slab. The nav is sticky and transparent at 72px, with the wordmark left, four links centered and Log in plus mint Start free right. The footer is a lifted, multi-column ruled sheet. At 375px, drop the display to 44px, stack cards 1-up and use 60px section gaps. The overall density is comfortable.

## Light-Serif Hierarchy

The discipline is that rank comes from size and family, never from stroke weight. Rhymes Display holds weight 300 at every one of its 16 uses, from 36px to 80px, while Inter tops out at 500 for 20–24px card titles. That leaves a deliberate gap: no element anywhere on the page is heavier than medium. It breaks the moment someone sets a pull quote in serif 600, uses Inter 700 for a pricing number, or adds a bold sans headline above the serif "for clarity". To extend the system, add new levels as new sizes on the existing ladder: 60px serif for a secondary hero, 24px Inter 500 for dense panels. Keep tracking negative only on the serif (-1.5px at 60px and above, -0.2px below).

## Chromatic Rationing

The page holds exactly two saturated hues against a field of warm neutrals. Mint #a7f3d0 appears on two elements, and Sunbeam #fdffa2 on one. The photography supplies color so the interface does not have to. The system breaks if the accent spreads: mint section buttons, yellow link underlines, colored feature icons, or a green gradient behind the testimonial. Each of these turns a rationed signal into decoration. To add status or category color, use tinted washes such as #d1fae5 under deep text such as #064e3b, at badge scale, 12px type and 10px radius. Pair every new hue with an existing neutral role and cap the page at one new saturated element per screen.

## Similar Brands

- **Attio** — Shares the Inter-driven interface and the 1px-ring-plus-contact-shadow elevation on near-white cards, but Attio keeps headlines in sans where Programa switches to a weight-300 serif.
- **Houzz Pro** — A direct category competitor in interior-design project software. Houzz uses a conventional saturated green brand and bold sans, which is exactly the convention Programa's two-hue budget rejects.
- **Notion** — Shares warm off-white surfaces, brown-black ink and hand-drawn, desk-object storytelling. Notion's illustration is line art, where Programa photographs real materials.
- **The Browser Company (Arc)** — Shares a collage-like, tactile hero with paper ephemera and an editorial serif against UI. Arc uses far more color and larger radii.
- **Cosmos** — Shares the curator-and-designer audience, large light serif headings and a near-colorless canvas that lets imagery carry all the hue.
